August, 2024

Author: Bela M. Trivedi
Bench: Bela M. Trivedi

 In The Supreme Court Of India
 Civil Original Jurisdiction
 Transfer Petition(s)(Civil) No(s). 1289/2024
 Blanka Jeetendra Varma Peti
 Versus
 Jeetendra Krishna Varma Resp
 O R D E R

1. By way of this petition filed under Section 25 of the Code of Civil Procedure, the petitioner-wife seeks transfer of the proceedings bearing Family Suit No.13 of 2020, titled JEETENDRA KRISHNA VARMA v. BLANKA JEETENDRA VARMA pending before the Court of the learned Principal Judge, Family Court of Navsari, Gujarat to the Family Court, Mumbai.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Court of the learned Principal Judge, Family Court of Navsari, Gujarat
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
3.

It is sought to be submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioner-wife that the parties to the proceedings never stayed in Navsari, Gujarat, and the Divorce Petition is filed by the respondent-husband in the 18:49:29 IST Reason:
Navsari Court, Gujarat only to harass the petitioner- wife.

She further submitted that right from the beginning, she had raised the said issues by filing application under Order 7 Rule 10 and after the dismissal of the same, she had filed an application seeking rejection of the divorce petition under Order 7 Rule 11(d) of CPC.

She further submitted that there are other proceedings filed by her against the respondent under Section 498A of the Indian Penal Code and the Domestic Violence Act which are pending before the 23rd Esplanade Court, Mumbai.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, the learned counsel for the respondent-husband has vehemently submitted that after fully participating before the Court at Navsari, Gujarat for four years and having failed in the application under Order 7 Rule 10, the petitioner has filed the present petition for transfer of case.

He also relied upon the decision of this Court in Abhilasha Gupta Versus Harimohan Gupta (2021) 9 SCC, 730 to submit that if the proceedings are already pending before the Navsari Court, Gujarat,
which are at an advanced stage, the Divorce Petition should not be transferred.

entities.text: Abhilasha Gupta Versus Harimohan Gupta (2021) 9 SCC, 730
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
5. Having regard to the submissions made by the learned counsel for the parties and the documents on record, we are of the opinion that though, the petitioner-wife had participated in the proceedings in the Divorce Petition which are pending at Navsari Court, Gujarat and though, we do not approve the indirect allegations made by the petitioner-wife in the rejoinder against the respondent- husband alleging his influence over the Court, considering the fact that the other proceedings i.e.
proceedings under Section-498A of IPC and the proceedings under the Domestic Violence Act, filed by the petitioner-wife, are pending before the Court at Mumbai, we are inclined to allow the present transfer petition.
6. Accordingly, as prayed for, Family Suit No.13 of 2020, titled JEETENDRA KRISHNA VARMA v.
BLANKA JEETENDRA VARMA
pending before the Court of the Principal Judge, Family Court of Navsari, Gujarat is ordered to be transferred to the Family Court, Mumbai.
7. Needless to say, the parties shall be at liberty to request the concerned Family Court at Mumbai for appearing through virtual mode.
If any such application or request is made, the same shall be considered by the concerned Court.
8. The transfer petition stands allowed accordingly.
9. The entire record pertaining to the Family Suit No.13 of 2020 shall be transmitted forthwith by the transferor court to the transferee court.
10. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.
